bookDiscrepancies.finding: Book blanket once-daily advice is not universal; reviewed clobetasol emollient cream is twice daily.
Exact product and indication matter; reviewed cream has a four-week psoriasis exception with age/area restrictions.
Do not treat the book vehicle ladder as a universal potency ranking; exact formulation controls.

Clarified rather than labeling book unequivocally wrong: one entire adult hand (both sides) differs from one flat handprint. Original1991 abstract supports variability, 1992 rule-of-hand title supports0.5g perFTU, and April2026 BAD leaflet supports two hand areas including fingers. Module now specifies5mm nozzle, flat handprints, approximation and both-sides distinction.

Book0.5% infant wording cannot authorize unsupervised infant use. Reviewed US1%label requires medical advice under2, for diaper rash, and for external anal itching under12. Module now distinguishes clinician-directed pediatric prescribing from OTC selection.
Book1-2/day statement is not a universal OTC label rule: reviewed Trifecta1%cream permits up to3-4/day. Module explains maximum is not mandatory frequency.
Book high group differs from current reviewed label medium range and JTF group3. New comparison explains classification context instead of unqualified high-potency claim.
Exact products differ: halcinonide cream2-3/day; diflorasone creamBID versus ointment1-3/day. Halobetasol lotion explicitly excludes scalp despite a scalp-friendly vehicle name.

Diflorasone cream labeling describes greater adrenal suppression than ointment in small studies; a potency hierarchy is not a systemic safety hierarchy. No universal vehicle ranking or safe dose inferred.
